module_title: Capital Market: Primary vs. Secondary Market and Securities
introduction: This level analyzes the mechanics of long-term investments. We will understand how companies issue shares for the very first time and how investors subsequently trade them on the stock exchange.

core_concepts.title: Primary Market (New Issue Market)
core_concepts.description: This is where 'new' securities (Shares/Bonds) are issued for the 'very first time'. When a company offers its shares to the public to raise fresh capital, it is called an IPO (Initial Public Offering). Here, money flows directly from the Investor to the Company.

core_concepts.title: Secondary Market (Stock Exchange)
core_concepts.description: This is the market where 'already issued' (second-hand) securities are traded. BSE and NSE are secondary markets. Here, shares are traded between 'Investor to Investor'. The original company gets ZERO new money from daily trading on the stock exchange.

core_concepts.title: Equity Shares vs. Preference Shares
core_concepts.description:
1. Equity Shares: The true owners of the company. They have 'Voting Rights', but there is absolutely no guarantee of getting a dividend. 
2. Preference Shares: They do not have voting rights, but they have the 'preference' (first right) to receive a 'fixed rate' of dividend out of the company's profits before equity shareholders get anything.

core_concepts.title: Debt Instruments (Bonds & Debentures)
core_concepts.description: This represents a 'Loan' given to the company, not ownership. Bond/Debenture holders do not care if the company makes a huge profit or a loss; they are legally entitled to receive their 'Fixed Interest' on time. Hence, they are much less risky than Equity.

important_entities.name: ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount)
important_entities.significance: A SEBI regulation ensuring that when you apply for an IPO, the money is not immediately deducted from your bank account. Instead, the funds are 'blocked'. The money is actually debited ONLY if shares are successfully allotted to you.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Question: 'Trading on the Stock Exchange directly creates new capital for the nation.' FALSE. 'Capital Formation' (new money entering businesses) ONLY happens in the 'Primary Market'. The Secondary Market merely provides 'Liquidity' for investors to exit.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Primary = Factory (New Goods), Secondary = Resale Shop (Used Goods)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The factory (Primary) makes money producing the good. The resale shop (Secondary) just transfers it between buyers.

exam_strategy_tips: Understanding the conceptual difference between the ASBA process and the 'Risk-Return Tradeoff' between Equity (High risk/High return) and Debt (Low risk/Fixed return) is critical for NISM Series V-A and VIII exams.
